note: Starter set of modern naval and defence topics. Verify anything time-sensitive against your own sources before a competition, and add your own current-knowledge questions in the Questions panel.

questions.prompt: Which ship is the lead ship of the US Navy's newest class of aircraft carriers?
hints: The class is named after her.
She is named for the 38th president.

questions.prompt: What is the primary mission of the P-8 Poseidon?
questions.answer: Maritime patrol, including anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare
hints: It is a fixed-wing aircraft built on a Boeing 737 airframe.
It replaced the P-3 Orion.

questions.prompt: Which variant of the F-35 is designed for aircraft carrier operations?
hints: The B variant is the short take-off and vertical landing one.
Carrier optimisation means larger wings and a stronger landing gear.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym AUKUS refer to?
questions.answer: A trilateral security partnership between Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States
hints: The name is built from the three countries.
It was announced in 2021 and includes a nuclear-powered submarine programme.

questions.prompt: What is the US Navy's carrier-based unmanned aerial refuelling aircraft called?
hints: It is unmanned and its job is to top up other aircraft.
Its name is a fish.

questions.prompt: Which class of US Navy destroyers carries the Aegis combat system and is the backbone of the surface fleet?
hints: It is named for a famous World War II destroyer admiral.
The class is abbreviated DDG-51.

questions.prompt: What is the mission of a littoral combat ship?
questions.answer: Operations in shallow coastal waters, including surface, anti-submarine and mine countermeasures missions
hints: 'Littoral' refers to the shore zone.
The class was designed to be fast, modular and small.

questions.prompt: Which aircraft provides carrier airborne early warning and control?
hints: It carries a large rotating radar dome on top.
It is a twin-turboprop aircraft.

questions.prompt: What is a tiltrotor aircraft, and which military transport is the best-known example?
questions.answer: An aircraft whose rotors tilt between helicopter and aeroplane flight; the V-22 Osprey
hints: It takes off like a helicopter and cruises like a plane.
The Marine Corps uses it as a medium-lift transport.

questions.prompt: In naval doctrine, what does 'distributed maritime operations' describe?
questions.answer: Spreading combat power across many networked, smaller formations rather than concentrating it in a few large units
hints: The opposite of putting everything in one place.
It relies on networking and long-range fires.

questions.prompt: Which class of stealth destroyers includes USS Zumwalt (DDG-1000)?
hints: The class takes its name from its lead ship.
Its distinctive feature is a low, angular superstructure.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a frigate and a destroyer in modern navies?
questions.answer: A destroyer is generally larger and more heavily armed for fleet air defence and strike, while a frigate is smaller and optimised for escort and patrol
hints: One is the larger, more capable escort.
The smaller of the two is the general-purpose workhorse.
